World’s Greatest Places

Each year, TIME makes a list of the World’s Greatest Places. TIME for Kids picks its favorites. This year’s list is all about adventure. There are amazing things to see and explore. Where would you go first?

Grand Museum

See 7,000 years of ancient history, all in one place. It’s possible at the new Grand Egyptian Museum. The museum is in Cairo, Egypt. It’s filled with thousands of treasures. It has every item found in King Tut’s tomb. The Pyramids of Giza are nearby. Visitors can walk there from the museum. —By Scott Laird

Catching Waves

At Surf Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates, every wave is perfect. It’s the world’s biggest wave pool. The waves are made by a machine. Pro surfer Kelly Slater helped develop the pool. Experienced surfers can ride big waves. Beginners can start small. Hop on board! —By Nicola Chilton

Witness the Wild

What do you see when you go to the zoo? You might see lions or giraffes walking around. Not at the Art Zoo Museum. It’s in Amsterdam, in the Netherlands. It’s not really a zoo. It’s a museum full of creatures that died long ago. They’ve been preserved, so you can get up close. Watch out for that T. Rex! —By Karen Burshtein

High in the Sky

The Huajiang Canyon Bridge is in China. It connects two mountains. It has the world’s highest bridge deck. Visitors can walk across the glass path, more than 2,000 feet above the ground. They can look down into the canyon below. Then they can take a glass elevator to the sky café.  —By Sucheta Rawal

Trek of a Lifetime

In Spanish, camino means “path.” El Camino de Costa Rica is much more than a path. It’s 174 miles long. It crosses Costa Rica, in South America. Hikers will climb mountains and go through rainforests. They might see iguanas and monkeys. —By Laura Dannen Redman

Peek into the Past

Murujuga Cultural Landscape is in Western Australia. This area is known for its ancient rock carvings. Some of them date back 50,000 years. They depict animals that are extinct, or no longer exist. And they show how people lived long ago. —By Michelle Tchea

On Two Wheels

The Ratnange Trail Center was made for mountain biking. Its trails are high up in Nepal. That’s a country in Asia. The tallest mountains in the world are there. (Mount Everest is one!) There are more than 43 trails for riders to tour. —By Samantha Falewée

Underwater Art

Put on your goggles! Reefline is an underwater sculpture park and snorkel trail. It’s in Miami Beach, Florida. Visitors swim through the artworks. Sea creatures do too. Some call this place a “mermaid playground.” —By Nora Walsh
